native_quality.interpretation: Zero changed fractions means zero pixels above the existing luminance threshold in each checked region; it does not assert byte-identical PNGs or every intermediate input state.

source_guarantees: Native frame requests enqueue a later record callback while immediately drawing and presenting the last recorded frame.
A present with no damage, unchanged dimensions, preserved target contents and no forcing overlay skips scene clear/replay.
The present still blits the preserved offscreen target into a newly acquired browser canvas texture and submits that blit.
WebGpuPresentSession with no replay or immediate draws returns before WebGpuFrame.Run, so no native scene-replay diagnostic line is emitted for that unchanged present.

Both SKCanvasElement and WebGpuCanvasElement invalidate through Compositor.InvalidateRender, which marks their own paint dirty and invalidates ancestor cached recordings. There is no host-specific unconditional scene replay here.

Opaque classification and mip-chain creation differ: the original uploaded texture scans alpha and creates mips; the persistent external render target defaults to unknown opacity and one mip. This is a source-proven difference, not a measured causal attribution.

separate_primary_context.separate_primary_elapsed_order: Composite median is lower than legacy median.
separate_primary_context.logging_diagnostic_elapsed_order: Legacy elapsed duration is lower than composite elapsed duration.

interpretation_and_limits: All four cases use the same explicit logging override, but logging can change scheduling and coalescing. This fixed-order, one-trial-per-mode diagnostic is not a primary speedup benchmark.

The historical same-package transport primary benchmark and these logging-enabled runs have opposite legacy/composite elapsed-time ordering. Do not infer a transport cause or multiply ratios across these experiments; primary timing evidence remains separate.

The native log counts are offscreen scene replay observations. Preserved offscreen contents can still be blitted and submitted to a newly acquired browser canvas texture without a WebGpuFrame.Run diagnostic line.
Browser callback and submission counts are not physical presentation counts, rendered FPS, or proof that every individual selection state reached the canvas.

Every frame-phases line averages 60 recordings. Its accumulated window may start before the sampled console range; all such lines may straddle the measurement boundaries. Gap is not GPU execution time.
The 60-op split within each mode matches that mode's selected and cleared canonical states. It does not establish an extra 60-op transport cost.

The original upload modes recorded fewer rows matching cleared-state canonical ops. The higher persistent/composite replay counts cannot be classified as redundant work from these data. Coalescing is a plausible interpretation, not a directly timestamp-proven cause.

Canonical pixel checks occur after the measured window and prove the two settled states only. Ops-based stage classification does not identify a per-input recording sequence or prove intermediate selected pixels.
Native elapsed stage fields are CPU-side observations from this logging run; they neither measure GPU execution directly nor isolate why primary timings changed.
The new legacy-composite implementation and current default are outside this historical artifact's source scope. No renderer promotion or current-source recovery is claimed.
